title: Interactions between monthly training volume, frequency and running distance per workout on marathon time
authors: Yamaguchi A, Shouji M, Akizuki A, Inoue K, Fukuie T, Sakuma K, et al.
population: Male recreational runners entered in the 2017 Hokkaido Marathon (587 completed a questionnaire, 494 finished)
findings: Within training-frequency subgroups, monthly volume, longest run distance (LRD) or average run distance (ARD) correlated significantly with marathon time, except in the subgroup training 2 times per week or less, where the ARD relationship was not significant.
In all monthly-volume subgroups, training frequency, LRD and ARD were not significantly related to marathon time.
Monthly volume correlated significantly with marathon time in the LRD >=21 km and ARD >=10 km subgroups (all P<0.01), not in the LRD 1-20 km and ARD <10 km subgroups.
Authors conclude monthly volume is the most important factor and that its influence is significant only if distance per workout exceeds a certain level.
limitations: Cross-sectional questionnaire; men only; self-reported; single race; finishers analysed; subgroup correlations, no causal dose-response; no effect sizes in the abstract.
implications: Treat volume as the primary progression variable, with typical session length of about 10 km or more and a longest run of at least 21 km before relying on more volume.
Do not expect extra weekly runs or a longer long run to add benefit at a fixed monthly volume; choose frequency by what the athlete can sustain.

verification.notes: Crossref (issued 2022-10-07), title, journal, first author match; Europe PMC year 2023 used. Researcher's finding 1 reworded to match the abstract (LRD/ARD, not only volume, correlated within frequency subgroups).
